introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (0565 Human Biology 1, June 2022, Ordinary Level, General Certificate of Education Board). Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; select only one answer. Non-programmable calculators are allowed.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one best answer, A, B, C or D. Questions 12-15 consist of two statements.

questions.enonce_markdown: How are humans different from other mammals?
questions.corrige_markdown: Humans, like most other mammals, have different kinds of teeth (heterodont), give birth to live young (viviparous) and have external ear flaps (pinnae). What really sets humans apart is the erect posture: we walk upright on two legs (bipedal) with the spine held vertically. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What is active transport?
questions.corrige_markdown: Active transport moves substances AGAINST the concentration gradient, that is from low to high concentration, using energy (ATP) from respiration and carrier proteins in the membrane. Options B and C describe diffusion (down the gradient, no energy). Option D is not a description of active transport either (osmosis moves water from high to low water potential and needs no energy). **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Movement of substances from an area of low concentration to that of high concentration
Movement of solutes from an area of high concentration to that of low concentration
Movement of substances from an area of high concentration to that of low concentration
Movement of water from an area of low water potential to that of high water potential.

questions.enonce_markdown: A cell organelle that plays a role in cell division is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The nucleus contains the chromosomes (DNA). During mitosis and meiosis the chromosomes are copied and shared between the daughter cells, and the nuclear division is the heart of cell division. Lysosomes digest materials, ribosomes make proteins and Golgi bodies process and secrete substances. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify the epithelium shown below.

![fig-1](gce-ol-human-biology-2022-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

(Courtsey of Roland Soper, GCSE, Human Biology).
questions.corrige_markdown: The diagram shows a single layer of tall, narrow, rectangular cells, much taller than they are wide, each with an elongated nucleus near the base, resting on a basement line. This is columnar epithelium (found in the lining of the small intestine). Cuboidal cells are as tall as wide, squamous cells are flat, and transitional epithelium is layered and stretchy (bladder). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A cell with 8 chromosomes undergoes mitosis. How many chromosomes will be found in each daughter cell?
questions.corrige_markdown: Mitosis produces two genetically identical daughter cells, each with the same chromosome number as the parent cell. Parent 8 chromosomes, so each daughter cell has 8. (4 would be the result of meiosis.) **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A natural fibre which is good for the production of sport wear is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Cotton is a natural plant fibre that is soft, absorbs sweat and lets the skin breathe, so it is the standard choice for sportswear. Wool is warm and heavy, silk is delicate and expensive, and linen creases easily and dries slowly. Note: wool, silk and linen are also natural fibres; cotton is the key most commonly expected. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which type of muscle makes up the walls of blood vessels?
questions.corrige_markdown: The walls of arteries and veins contain smooth (involuntary, non-striated) muscle, which contracts slowly and automatically to change the diameter of the vessel. Cardiac muscle is only in the heart, and skeletal muscle (which is striated) moves the bones. Striated muscle includes skeletal and cardiac muscle, so D is wrong. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following reduces friction at the joint?
questions.corrige_markdown: At a synovial joint, the smooth cartilage covering the bone ends and the lubricating synovial fluid reduce friction between the moving bones. Tendons join muscle to bone and ligaments join bone to bone; they hold and move the joint but do not reduce friction. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The chamber of the ear filled with fluid is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The inner ear (cochlea, semicircular canals and vestibule) is filled with fluid (perilymph and endolymph). The outer ear and the middle ear contain air, and the Eustachian tube is an air-filled tube linking the middle ear to the throat. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The ions responsible for the conduction of nerve impulses along the neurone are:
questions.corrige_markdown: A nerve impulse is a wave of depolarisation: Na+ ions rush into the axon and then K+ ions leave it, which is how the action potential travels along the neurone. Calcium acts at the synapse (neurotransmitter release), not along the axon. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Below is the diagram of the skin.

![fig-2](gce-ol-human-biology-2022-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)

( Courtesy of DG Macheans, Introduction to Biology).

Identify the part that regulates body temperature.
questions.corrige_markdown: Label 5 is the coiled sweat gland in the dermis with its duct running up to a pore. When the body is hot, sweat is secreted onto the skin and its evaporation cools the body, so the sweat gland regulates temperature. Label 4 is a sebaceous (oil) gland beside the hair follicle, label 6 is the fatty tissue below the dermis (insulation and storage) and label 2 is the epidermis. Identification relies on the unlabelled drawing. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 12-15 consist of two statements. Read through the statements and then choose A, B, C or D.

| First statement | Second statement |
|---|---|
| The afferent arteriole which brings blood to the glomerulus is wider in diameter than the efferent arteriole which takes blood away | The blood in the glomerulus is under high pressure for ultrafiltration |
questions.corrige_markdown: Both statements are true. Because the afferent arteriole is wider than the efferent one, blood enters the glomerulus faster than it can leave, which builds up the high hydrostatic pressure needed to force small molecules out of the blood (ultrafiltration). The second statement therefore explains the first. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: If both statements are true and the second explains the first
If both statements are true but the second does not explain the first
If the first statement is false and the second is true

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 12-15 consist of two statements. Read through the statements and then choose A, B, C or D.

| First statement | Second statement |
|---|---|
| The visible traits of an organism constitute its genotype | Albinism is a sex-linked recessive trait in humans |
questions.corrige_markdown: Both statements are false. The visible traits of an organism are its phenotype (the genotype is the genetic make-up, the combination of alleles). Albinism is an autosomal recessive condition, not a sex-linked one. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: If both statements are true and the second explains the first
If both statements are true but the second does not explain the first
If the first statement is false and the second is true

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 12-15 consist of two statements. Read through the statements and then choose A, B, C or D.

| First statement | Second statement |
|---|---|
| Photosynthesis uses O$_2$ and produces CO$_2$ | Autotrophs constitute the first trophic level of a food chain |
questions.corrige_markdown: The first statement is false: photosynthesis uses CO$_2$ and water and produces glucose and O$_2$ (the reverse of what is stated). The second statement is true: green plants and other autotrophs (producers) form the first trophic level. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: If both statements are true and the second explains the first
If both statements are true but the second does not explain the first
If the first statement is false and the second is true

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 12-15 consist of two statements. Read through the statements and then choose A, B, C or D.

| First statement | Second statement |
|---|---|
| The presence of protein in a food sample will give a red precipitate | NaOH and copper II sulphate are used to test for the presence of proteins in a food sample |
questions.corrige_markdown: The first statement is false: the biuret test for protein gives a purple (violet) colour, not a red precipitate (a red-brown precipitate is the result of the Benedict test for reducing sugars). The second statement is true: the biuret test uses sodium hydroxide followed by copper(II) sulphate solution. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: If both statements are true and the second explains the first
If both statements are true but the second does not explain the first
If the first statement is false and the second is true

questions.enonce_markdown: Cells that play a role in bone formation are:
questions.corrige_markdown: Osteoblasts are the bone-forming cells which lay down the new bone matrix. Osteoclasts break bone down, osteocytes are mature bone cells that maintain the bone, and chondroblasts form cartilage. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When alleles express themselves equally in the phenotype, the condition is referred to as:
questions.corrige_markdown: In codominance both alleles are fully and equally expressed in the heterozygote (e.g. blood group AB). Sex linkage concerns genes on the sex chromosomes, dominance means one allele masks the other, and "incomplete codominance" is not a standard term. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify the endocrine gland below which secretes a hormone that regulates blood sugar level.

![fig-3](gce-ol-human-biology-2022-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)

(Adapted from DG Macheans, Introduction to Biology).
questions.corrige_markdown: The hormones insulin and glucagon, which regulate the blood sugar level, are made by the islets of Langerhans of the pancreas. In the diagram 1 is the pituitary gland in the head, 2 the thyroid gland in the neck, 3 the pancreas lying beside the stomach, 4 the adrenal gland above the kidney, and 5 and 6 the gonads. So the answer is 3. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these blood groups is a universal recipient?
questions.corrige_markdown: Group AB blood has neither anti-A nor anti-B antibodies in the plasma, so it can receive blood of any ABO group: it is the universal recipient. Group O is the universal donor. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Immunity acquired through vaccination is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown: A vaccine contains weakened or dead pathogens or their antigens, which make the body produce its own antibodies and memory cells: this is ACTIVE immunity, and since it is given deliberately it is ARTIFICIAL. Passive immunity means antibodies are received ready-made (e.g. across the placenta or in breast milk). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An enzyme in the duodenum that acts on fats is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Pancreatic lipase, in the pancreatic juice that enters the duodenum, digests fats (emulsified by bile) into fatty acids and glycerol. Amylase acts on starch, trypsinogen is the inactive form of a protease, and enterokinase activates trypsinogen. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The structure which prevents food from entering the wind pipe (trachea) is the:
questions.corrige_markdown: When we swallow, the epiglottis, a flap of cartilage, closes over the glottis (the opening of the trachea), so food goes down the oesophagus. The glottis is the opening itself and the cartilage rings keep the trachea open. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A Centre where old people are kept and taken care of is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: Geriatrics is the branch of medicine dealing with the old, so a geriatric home is a centre where elderly people are looked after. A post-natal clinic cares for mothers and babies after birth and an antenatal clinic for pregnant women. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The causative agent of typhoid fever is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Typhoid fever is caused by the bacterium Salmonella typhi (written Salmonella typhosus in the paper), spread by contaminated food and water. Tubercle bacillus causes tuberculosis, Treponema pallidum syphilis and Corynebacterium diphtheriae diphtheria. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Fraternal twins result from:
questions.corrige_markdown: Fraternal (non-identical) twins develop when two ova are released and each is fertilised by a different sperm. Identical twins come from one fertilised ovum that splits in two. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The process by which the liver converts excess amino acids into urea is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: Excess amino acids cannot be stored. In the liver the amino group (-NH$_2$) is removed (deamination) and converted to ammonia and then to urea, while the remaining carbon part is used as energy. Transamination only moves the amino group from one acid to another. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which component of cigarette smoke causes cancer?
questions.corrige_markdown: Tar contains carcinogens (cancer-causing chemicals) that damage the cells of the lungs and airways. Nicotine is the addictive drug and carbon monoxide reduces the oxygen carried by the blood. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The diagram below is that of the motor neurone.

![fig-4](gce-ol-human-biology-2022-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_4.png)

(Courtsey of AG Toole *et al*., Advance Level Biology Course Companion)

Which numbered structure carries impulses towards the muscle?

*Options as printed:* A) 1   B) 3   C) 4   D) 5
questions.corrige_markdown: In a motor neurone the impulse travels from the cell body along the AXON to the nerve endings at the muscle (the arrow points in the direction of conduction). The structure that carries the impulse is therefore the axon (not the nucleus 1 and not the cell body 2). In the drawing, however, lines 3, 4 and 5 all end on the axon region (3 at a gap between two Schwann cells, 4 at a Schwann cell nucleus, 5 at the axon under a Schwann cell), so no single option can be identified without doubt. The question is left open for self-assessment: the answer is the axon.

questions.enonce_markdown: The monthly process in humans that releases an egg from the ovary is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: Ovulation is the release of a mature egg from the ovary (about day 14 of the cycle). Menstruation is the loss of the uterus lining, implantation is the attachment of the embryo to the uterus wall and gestation is the period of pregnancy. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these blood components is biconcave in shape and lacks a nucleus?
questions.corrige_markdown: Erythrocytes (red blood cells) are biconcave discs without a nucleus, which gives more room for haemoglobin and a large surface for gas exchange. Thrombocytes (platelets) are cell fragments without a nucleus but not biconcave, while lymphocytes and monocytes are white cells with a nucleus. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The structures used by an adult tapeworm to attach itself onto the walls of the host's small intestine are the:

*Options as printed:* A) Rostellum and suckers   B) Hooks and suckers   C) Proglottids and hooks   D) Hooks and rostellum
questions.corrige_markdown: The scolex (head) of an adult tapeworm (Taenia solium) has suckers and a crown of hooks carried on a rostellum; these hold the worm to the intestine wall. The usual textbook answer is "hooks and suckers" (B), but A (rostellum and suckers) and D (hooks and rostellum) also name real attachment structures of the scolex. Proglottids are the body segments and are not used for attachment (C is wrong). Because more than one option is defensible, the question is left open for self-assessment.

questions.enonce_markdown: In the carbon cycle the process that converts carbon from fossil fuel to carbon dioxide is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Burning (combustion) of fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas releases the carbon stored in them as carbon dioxide. Respiration and decomposition act on living or dead organisms, and fossilization is the formation of fossil fuel, the opposite process. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: At what stage of the purification process of water is alum or iron III chloride added to water?
questions.corrige_markdown: Alum or iron(III) chloride is a coagulant: it makes the tiny suspended particles clump together into heavy flocs which settle at the bottom of the sedimentation tank. Screening removes large objects, filtration removes the remaining small particles and chlorination kills germs. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The hormone responsible for maintaining the lining of the uterus during pregnancy is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: Progesterone (from the corpus luteum, then the placenta) keeps the uterus lining thick and well supplied with blood and prevents menstruation during pregnancy. LH triggers ovulation, FSH stimulates follicle growth and prolactin stimulates milk production. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The term homeostasis refers to:
questions.corrige_markdown: Homeostasis is the maintenance of a constant INTERNAL environment, i.e. the composition of blood and tissue fluid (temperature, water, glucose, pH...). A and C name only one example each, and D is wrong because the external environment cannot be kept constant by the body. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: The maintenance of a constant body temperature
The maintenance of a constant composition of blood and tissue fluid
The maintenance of the water content of the body fluids
The maintenance of a constant external environment

questions.enonce_markdown: Choose the structure of the skin that is sensitive to heat and cold.
questions.corrige_markdown: Free nerve endings in the skin respond to temperature changes (and pain). Meissner's corpuscles detect light touch, Pacinian corpuscles pressure, and the hair plexus (nerve network around hair follicles) detects hair movement. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following occurs during Expiration?
questions.corrige_markdown: During expiration the external intercostal muscles and the diaphragm relax, the ribs move down and in, the diaphragm domes upwards, the volume of the thorax decreases and the pressure rises, pushing air out. B and C describe inspiration. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: The volume of the thorax increases
The volume of the thorax remains the same

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the blood vessels below that have valves in them.
questions.corrige_markdown: Veins carry blood at low pressure back to the heart and have semilunar valves that prevent backflow. Capillaries and arterioles have no valves, and venules (small veins) have none either. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The pedigree below illustrates the sex-linked recessive trait known as haemophilia in a family.

![fig-5](gce-ol-human-biology-2022-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_5.png)

What is the genotype of Alice?
questions.corrige_markdown: The key shows Alice as a carrier female (shaded circle): she has a normal phenotype but carries the haemophilia allele, so she is heterozygous X$^H$X$^h$. This agrees with the family: her son Alexis is haemophiliac (X$^h$Y), and he must have received X$^h$ from his mother since his father Jude is normal (X$^H$Y). X$^H$Y and X$^h$Y are male genotypes and X$^H$X$^H$ would be a non-carrier. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A disease condition in which the body does not have enough red blood cells is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Anaemia is a shortage of red blood cells or haemoglobin (for example from iron deficiency). Haemophilia is failure of blood clotting, arteriosclerosis is hardening of the arteries and thrombosis is a blood clot in a vessel. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A cold compress (ice pack) is applied on the affected joint of a victim of a dislocation as a first aid measure to:
questions.corrige_markdown: Cold narrows blood vessels and numbs the nerve endings, which reduces pain, swelling and inflammation around the injured joint. It does not hold the bones in place (that is done by immobilisation with a sling or splint). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which enzymes are contained in intestinal juice?
questions.corrige_markdown: Intestinal juice (succus entericus) contains maltase and sucrase (carbohydrases), lipase and erepsin (peptidases). Ptyalin is salivary amylase, pepsin is made in the stomach and trypsin comes from the pancreas. Only option B has three enzymes that all belong to the intestinal juice. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Identify one cause of miscarriage in human females.

*Options as printed:* A) Consumption of prescribed drugs   B) Insufficient secretion of oestrogen   C) Excessive cigarette smoking   D) Insufficient secretin of progesterone
questions.corrige_markdown: Miscarriage is the loss of the embryo before it can survive. The classic hormonal cause is too little progesterone, which fails to maintain the uterus lining (D). However, heavy cigarette smoking is also a recognised cause of miscarriage (C), so two options are defensible; prescribed drugs (A) are normally safe and low oestrogen (B) is not the usual cause. The question is left open for self-assessment (D and C).

questions.enonce_markdown: A disease which spreads worldwide affecting many people at a time is known as a/an:
questions.corrige_markdown: A pandemic spreads over many countries or continents. An epidemic is limited to a region or country, an endemic disease is always present in a particular area and a sporadic disease occurs only occasionally and in a few isolated cases. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What determines sex in humans?
questions.corrige_markdown: Sex is determined by the sex chromosomes (heterosomes or allosomes): XX gives a female and XY a male. Autosomes are the other 22 pairs of chromosomes and do not determine sex. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify one hazard of ultraviolet radiation in humans.
questions.corrige_markdown: Too much ultraviolet radiation damages the DNA of skin cells and can cause skin cancer (also sunburn and cataract). Obesity, miscarriage and deafness are not linked to UV radiation. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which class of food is responsible for growth and repair of body tissues?
questions.corrige_markdown: Proteins (body-building foods) supply the amino acids needed to build new cells and repair damaged tissues. Carbohydrates give energy, and vitamins and minerals protect the body and regulate processes. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In conditions of high salt concentration in the blood:
questions.corrige_markdown: A high salt concentration (low water potential) of the blood is detected by the hypothalamus, which makes the pituitary gland release ADH. ADH makes the collecting ducts more permeable, so MORE water is reabsorbed and a small volume of concentrated urine is produced. A and D are the reverse, and C is not the response. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: No ADH is secreted by the pituitary gland
ADH is secreted by the pituitary gland
More salts are absorbed along the nephron
Less water is absorbed along the nephron

questions.enonce_markdown: An important rule of good hygiene is to:
questions.corrige_markdown: Trimming the finger and toe nails regularly stops dirt and germs from collecting under them. Exercise should be regular, not occasional, taking drugs regularly is harmful, and bathing straight after exercise is not a rule of hygiene (it is better to cool down first). **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Exercise the body once in a while
Bathe immediately after exercising the body
Trim finger and toe nails regularly

questions.enonce_markdown: A benefit of a playground to the community is:
questions.corrige_markdown: A playground gives the community a place to train and practise games and keep fit. The other options describe misuse or harmful activities and are not benefits. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: A place for the perpetuation of violence
A place for the training and practice of games
A place for the organizing of religious crusades
A place for the lodging of drug addicts
